title: Gemini on your Google Home talking to itself? A fix is on the way
summary: Gemini can mistake its own voice for yours, triggering loops and duplicate commands.
body: TL;DR Gemini Live can hear its own voice on some Google Home devices, causing it to interrupt itself and get stuck in a loop. Users have reported crashes, repeated responses, and Gemini creating duplicate timers after hearing its own confirmation. Google has acknowledged the bug and is rolling out improvements, although it hasn’t provided a completion timeline. Earlier this year, some Android Auto users watched Gemini Live hear its own voice and spiral into a conversation with itself. In-car audio setups emerged as a possible culprit, but similar behavior is now surfacing on some Google Home devices. The good news? Google has now acknowledged the bug and says improvements are rolling out. The issue surfaced on Reddit after a Google Home user said Gemini Live had become unusable. Responding last Friday, the official Google Nest Community account confirmed that Live Mode was interrupting itself on some devices and said improvements were rolling out.

title: After Gemini, another Google app may be coming to macOS
summary: Evidence within the latest Google Play Services update suggests the Google app could soon land on macOS.
body: TL;DR A standalone Google app could be in the works for Mac desktops. Android Authority has found a direct reference to a macOS app within the latest Google Play Services update. This comes months after Google rolled out the app for Windows computers, along with a Gemini app for Macs. A large chunk of Google’s consumer apps, including Photos, Drive, Gemini, Sheets, and Docs, are already available for Apple’s iOS and iPadOS platforms. However, the list is smaller for macOS. The arrival of a standalone Gemini app has changed that to some extent, and we’re now seeing early evidence that the Google app may be next on that list. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: Samsung may pull an Apple and make the Galaxy S26 series pricier
summary: Rising memory costs may finally be catching up with Samsung.
body: TL;DR Samsung could reportedly raise prices for every Galaxy S26 model in South Korea by 149,600 won (about $110) on October 1. The unusual increase would arrive nearly seven months after the phones launched, amid soaring RAM and component costs. Samsung says it is reviewing its pricing but has made no final decision, with no indication of a US increase. When Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max , higher prices than last year’s models felt inevitable. But few expected Apple to use the launch to raise prices on its older iPhones . Now, Android’s biggest name may be reading from the same playbook, as a Korean outlet claims Samsung is considering an unusual post-launch price hike for the Galaxy S26 series. According to Hans Economy , a South Korean carrier has informed retailers that wholesale prices for every Galaxy S26 model will rise by 149,600 won (about $110) on October 1. That would be unusual because Samsung launched the phones in March, putting the alleged price hike nearly seven months into their life cycle.

title: Apple’s Handoff lets two iPhones share one number, but it won’t come cheap
summary: T-Mobile will put your number on a second iPhone, but for the right price.
body: TL;DR Apple’s new Handoff feature, which lets you use the same number on two iPhones, won’t be free. T-Mobile, the only carrier to support Handoff at launch, will cost an extra $5 per month. T-Mobile says both phones should be able to use crucial features like calling, SMS, data, and even T-Satellite. The iPhone 18 Pro , which Apple announced last week, lacks any significant upgrade other than its new chip. Even the new camera Apple touted adds a feature Android brands have had for years . Irrespective of that, something that makes the iPhone 18 Pro truly compelling is the ability to use another iPhone with the same phone number, much like you would with an Apple Watch. This feature is called “Handoff, ” and it currently requires carrier support. That means only a handful of carriers will initially support it and may charge you more for the service, especially as they’re giving you the opportunity to sell you another line. At launch, T-Mobile is the only carrier in the US to support Handoff, while Verizon is likely to add support in the coming months.

body: TL;DR Super Smash Bros Melee has been unofficially ported to Windows. This comes just days after the game was fully decompiled, opening the door to fan ports. body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s Advanced Protection mode currently clubs several security features that users can’t opt out of individually, except for Intrusion Logging. We’ve now discovered that Google is preparing to move USB Protection, Intrusion Detection, and Unsecured Wi-Fi Networks into an optional “Expert features” section. The change could give users more flexibility while retaining Advanced Protection’s strongest protections for those who want them. Google introduced Advanced Protection with Android 16 as a way for users to enable some of the strongest security and privacy protections on their devices. The feature is designed to protect against everything from harmful apps and online attacks to unauthorized access and other security risks.

title: Could Galaxy S27 Ultra bring zoom camera upgrades? New leak has bad news
summary: Those hoping for more impressive zoom camera hardware might be disappointed.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR A veteran leaker has dismissed claims that the Galaxy S27 Ultra could get a 4x camera in lieu of the existing 50MP 5x shooter. The source says Samsung will continue to use a 50MP 5x camera, as seen on the S24 Ultra, S25 Ultra, and S26 Ultra. This might be the only telephoto camera on the S27 Ultra, as Samsung was previously tipped to ditch the 3x camera. Two sources recently suggested that Samsung could bring a major change to the Galaxy S27 Ultra zoom cameras. However, a trusted leaker has now poured cold water on these claims. Tipster phonefuturist claimed late last month that Samsung was testing a 50MP 4x sensor (1/1.9-inch) on the Galaxy S27 Ultra. This was echoed by fellow user GalaxyFlash2025 , who claimed early this month that the S27 Ultra would ditch the 3x and 5x cameras in favor of a 4x 1/1.9-inch sensor. This 4x sensor would be larger than the S26 Ultra ‘s 3x and 5x cameras.

title: 6 reasons I still haven’t bought a Google TV projector (and why I may never get one)
summary: Google TV projectors are tempting, but I'm not sure they're right for me.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority The cheap projector market really took off a few years ago, and the market was suddenly flooded with units ranging from $50 to well over $500. During that time, I invested in a cheap but decent little unit for around $100 that had HDMI support and came with a Roku in the box. While certainly not capable of replacing a TV at this level, it was a great way to watch movies outdoors and gave me a taste of what projector life might be. I reasoned that if these cheap units were this capable, then a real higher-priced projector could likely take me much further. Recently, our living room TV has started showing signs that its days are numbered, and I’ve once again started researching the best projectors . I have to admit I strongly considered a Google TV projector, as many recent models have received praise from critics and users alike. Not to mention, these units have Google TV baked in, so there’s less setup and no extra equipment needed. The more I looked into it, though, the more convinced I became that I might be better off spending the same $500-$1000 on a “dumb” projector.

Android 16 introduced resizable tiles , while Android 17 added things like separate Wi-Fi and mobile data controls , alongside a more customizable layout. title: My Pixel was overheating and stuttering until I made these 5 tweaks
summary: Now my Pixel is as chill as me.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority As much as I love my Pixel 10, it has some glaring issues . The big one is overheating, and frankly, that applies to all Pixel phones in general. Sure, every phone runs warm occasionally, but Pixels seem to be more prone to it than most. I’ve had mine overheat at times even when I wasn’t gaming, using the camera, or plugged into Android Auto. Also, overheating isn’t something you can just ignore. It affects how the phone feels in your hand, how it performs, and even how fast it charges. So instead of waiting for some magic update from Google or upgrading to a new phone, I decided to actually do something about it. It took some effort, but my Pixel no longer runs as hot as it used to.

Streaming subscriptions can add up surprisingly quickly when you’re a student, especially if you’re juggling several of them just to keep up with different shows. Disney is now making two of its biggest services a lot cheaper for college students. title: Meta’s Project Phoenix just leaked, and it looks nothing like a Quest
summary: Project Phoenix looks ready to make bulky headsets feel very yesterday.
body: TL;DR Images found inside Meta’s HorizonOS Prescription Lens app appear to reveal the rumored Project Phoenix headset ahead of Meta Connect on September 23. Phoenix looks more like chunky glasses than a traditional Quest headset, with glasses-style nose pads, sensors around the temples, and a separate compute puck. We still haven’t seen Phoenix properly from the front or on someone’s face, leaving big questions about its size, appearance, and overall design. Meta Connect kicks off on September 23, and we may have just gotten an early peek at one of the more interesting devices Meta could be preparing to talk about. UploadVR has spotted images of Meta’s rumored Project Phoenix headset inside the HorizonOS Prescription Lens app. While they don’t show the full device, they reveal enough to suggest Phoenix won’t be another Quest-style headset . Instead, Meta appears to be going for something much slimmer. From the angles shown, Phoenix looks more like chunky glasses than a conventional VR headset. Nose pads hold the device in place, while what appear to be sensors sit around the temples. The overall look immediately reminds me of XREAL Aura glasses , which use a similar setup.

This and several other images of both visually and scientifically interesting galaxies were released by NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes. Chandra X-ray data (magenta) pinpoint powerful black hole activity and hot gas, while optical data (blue and white) from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and infrared data from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope illuminate vast stellar nurseries hidden behind interstellar dust. Systems like II Zw 096 show us how powerful galaxy collisions shaped the early universe. See more galaxy photos from Chandra. title: I tried out the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Google still can’t convince me to buy a foldable
summary: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is better than ever. But is it finally worth it? Ehh...
body: It’s been a while since I last used a book-style foldable . My previous dalliance was the OPPO Find N2 back in 2022, and while I was impressed by how far the form factor had already come, I ultimately didn’t see enough reason to make the switch. Like many other potential converts, the drawbacks simply weren’t worth the small benefits. Four years on, I’m back to find out whether things have finally changed with the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold. I’ve spent plenty of time with Pixel Pro flagships in the intervening years and have generally been a fan of Google’s software, cameras, and even some of its latest AI-focused approaches. But does that familiar Pixel formula work when you double the screen and fold the whole thing in half? More importantly, has the foldable finally become something I actually want to use every day?

title: 5 Android phones you should buy instead of the Google Pixel 11 Pro
summary: Google has plenty of competition.
body: The Pixel 11 Pro is precisely what I thought it would be, and it’s still been as divisive as ever. Early reviews have been positive, and it’s clear Google leaned into what has made its Pixel lineup more successful over the last few years. The phones are pleasant and easy to use, ideal for beginners switching over to Android for the first time. However, it’s also never been more apparent that Pixels aren’t for enthusiasts who stare at benchmarks before buying a phone. And the Pixel 11 Pro has legitimate weaknesses. title: The iPhone 18 Pro camera is already years behind 2026 Android phones
summary: The iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture camera sounds impressive, but it's not enough for me.
body: Much of this week’s talk about Apple’s new releases centers on the brand’s first foldable—the iPhone Duo . But as a practical individual, I imagine a lot more consumers will be looking at the iPhone 18 Pro series and pondering whether there’s enough new hardware to justify the price hikes. While there are some key tweaks to processing power and new camera software tools, the iPhone’s latest innovation is a return to variable-aperture technology, ranging from f/1.48 to f/4, that Android rivals trialed and abandoned years ago. If this is seriously the best Apple can do to catch up with China’s best camera phones, I can’t see serious photographers like myself rushing to switch to the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max.

title: Your Pixel phone quietly got a new feature to help prevent motion sickness — here’s how to use it
summary: Motion Assist to save the day.
body: Motion sickness is not a fun thing to deal with. While I don’t personally struggle with it, I’ve known people who do, and it seems like it can be pretty unbearable at times. Thankfully, if you have a Pixel phone, you now have a clever new feature that can help keep motion sickness at bay. The feature is called “ Motion Assist ,” and it works by displaying small dots around the edge of your screen that move according to your phone’s gyroscope and accelerometer. So, if you’re riding in a car, the dots will follow the same motion/movement as the vehicle.

title: Android just made switching password managers a whole lot safer and easier
summary: Your passwords finally get a safer ride to their new home.
body: TL;DR Android is making it easier and safer to move passwords and passkeys between supported password managers. The new system removes the need to export your password vault as a potentially unencrypted file and manually import it elsewhere. Password transfers currently work with Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden, and Dashlane, with more services coming later. Passwords are basically the keys to our digital lives. They protect everything from our emails and social media accounts to banking apps and personal photos, so the last thing you want is to accidentally leave them exposed. Unfortunately, that can become a concern when you decide to switch password managers. Right now, you may have to export your entire vault as a file, save it to your device, and then import it into your new password manager . Worse, that exported file can be unencrypted, which means all those usernames and passwords you’ve spent years protecting could temporarily sit together in a regular file on your phone. You also have to remember to delete it once you’re done.
